Algeria Imposes Temporary Export Restrictions on Oil & Gas, Industry Faces Disruption

ALGIERS, June 20 – Algerian authorities have imposed temporary restrictions on oil and gas exports as part of new trade-policy measures aimed at securing domestic energy supplies, officials said Thursday, prompting immediate disruption in the Oil & Gas Producers industry.

The Ministry of Energy announced late Wednesday that the export of certain crude oil and liquefied natural gas products would be limited for at least 30 days, citing increased domestic demand and the need to stabilize national reserves. The move has affected several major industry players, including Societe Nationale de I Electricite & Du Gaz SpA.

“The current global environment and rising local consumption have made it essential to prioritize Algerian needs,” a ministry spokesperson said in a statement. “These restrictions are temporary but necessary.”

According to industry sources, shipments of oil and gas from key production facilities in Hassi Messaoud and Skikda have already been delayed. Abdelkader Benali, an analyst at the Algiers-based Maghreb Energy Forum, said, “Export volumes are likely to drop by as much as 35% this month. The impact is being felt across the sector, with companies facing logistical and financial challenges.”

A spokesperson for Societe Nationale de I Electricite & Du Gaz SpA confirmed that the company is adjusting schedules and reallocating resources in response to the new restrictions. “We are working with authorities to ensure compliance while minimizing disruption to our commitments,” the spokesperson said.

The Algerian Oil and Gas Producers Association warned the measures could hurt investment and strain relationships with international buyers if the restrictions persist. Talks between industry representatives and government officials are ongoing, with no timeline yet for the complete lifting of the export limits.
